;Business and economy
*A [[U.S. dollar|US$]]5 billion [[class action]] lawsuit is filed against [[Alphabet Inc.]] and [[Google]], alleging the company violates users' [[right to privacy]] by tracking them in [[Google Chrome|Chrome]]'s [[Private browsing|incognito mode]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-52887340 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
**India approves the use of [[remdesivir]] to treat emergency [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases that require immediate attention. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/06/02/india-approves-emergency-use-of-remdesivir-to-treat-covid-19-patients.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]

;International relations
*[[Philippines–United States relations]]
**[[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] suspends for six months the termination of the [[Philippines–United States Visiting Forces Agreement]]. [[Secretary of Foreign Affairs (Philippines)|Foreign Affairs Secretary]] [[Teodoro Locsin Jr.]] says the decision comes due to "political and other developments in the region". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/philippines-backtracks-termination-military-deal-200602142554480.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**[[U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] announces sanctions on four shipping firms for transporting oil from Venezuela. Three firms are based in the [[Marshall Islands]] and another in [[Greece]]. Venezuelan Foreign Minister [[Jorge Arreaza]] responds by saying Pompeo has a "criminal obsession" with Venezuela. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-venezuela-oil/u-s-sanctions-four-shipping-firms-for-transporting-venezuelan-oil-idUSKBN2392BC?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests in Washington, D.C.]]
**[[James N. Miller]], former U.S. [[Under Secretary of Defense for Policy]], announces his resignation from the [[Defense Science Board]], citing disagreement with the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]'s actions against protestors in [[Washington, D.C.]] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2020/06/02/secretary-esper-you-violated-your-oath-aiding-trumps-photo-op-thats-why-im-resigning/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*In [[France]], despite being banned by the police headquarters, a demonstration organized by the Justice pour Adama movement in [[Paris (France)|Paris]] gathered 20,000 participants. They were protesting for charges against police officers who had killed a young black man, Adama Traoré, during his arrest in 2016. They also demonstrated in support of the Black Lives Matter movement in the United States, and in protest against police violence against black and Arab individuals in France in general. Some clashes occur at the end of the event. Other smaller demonstrations took place in the towns of [[Lyon (France)|Lyon]], [[Marseille (France)|Marseille]] and [[Lille, France|Lille]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200603-france-urges-calm-after-tense-protest-over-black-man-s-death (France 24)]
